documents.description:
**Why.** The design-spec artifact `cfd0e75b` is the canonical GUI↔TUI parity reference (the white-ladder glyphs, the board/detail side-by-sides, the drift-gate story). Recreating it as a native Barkpark PortableDoc paper means it renders identically across all 9 renderers and is governed by the same tokens and drift gate as the surfaces it documents — the spec eats its own dog food.

**Approach.** Keep the real 3-level tree: `parity-page` → the 7 `parity-sN` section docs (s1-alive … s7-identical, which are both phase-band headers AND real deliverables) → one component leaf per figure/component, authored as PortableDoc blocks. Each leaf inherits its section's phase label.

**Out of scope.** The surface *builds* themselves (Studio/Web/TUI/PortableDoc adopting tokens) live under `aesthetic-unification-epic`; this epic only recreates the SPEC artifact as a paper.

purpose.why: The larger goal is GUI–TUI parity paper — express the durable cross-surface design doctrine as native PortableDoc that proves its own rendering contract. The concrete problem was that the original external artifact was unrecoverable and screenshots would not exercise the product's real document system. Authoring the hierarchy and every figure as native PortableDoc sections and components was the correct intervention because the specification can dogfood renderer parity and remain editable, testable, and linkable inside Barkpark. If omitted, the doctrine depends on a dead external artifact and cannot prove that its own design language works across surfaces.
